headline: Repeatedly remove courses with no remaining prerequisites
statement: There are numCourses labeled courses. Each pair [a,b] requires b before a. Return whether every course can be completed.
intuition: A course is ready when none of its prerequisites remain unfinished. Put all ready courses in a queue. Taking one removes a requirement from its dependent courses, which may make them ready. If some courses never become ready, they are blocked by a cycle of requirements.
approach: Build edges from prerequisite to dependent and count incoming edges.
Take each ready course, reduce its dependents' indegrees, and enqueue newly ready courses.
correctness: Every removed course has no prerequisites among the unremoved courses, so the removal order is legal. If all courses are removed, that order proves feasibility. Otherwise every remaining node has an incoming edge from another remaining node; repeatedly following predecessors in a finite graph reaches a cycle, which prevents completion.
bruteForce: Try all course permutations and check their ordering. Topological removal determines feasibility in linear graph time.

complexity.explanation: Adjacency lists hold edges; indegrees and the ready queue hold courses.

pitfalls: Include isolated courses in the initial queue.
A disconnected cyclic component still makes the answer false.
